title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction: Context: In E510 Euler studies a heavy column buckling under its own weight. As a warm-up he replaces the continuous elastic column with a discrete model. Two rigid bars CA and CB, each of length a and weight M, are joined at the middle C by an elastic joint (a rotational spring E e). The ends A (top) and B (bottom) are held on the vertical line AB, and a horizontal force C acts at the joint. On this page he: (1) Linearizes for small deflection angle θ = ∠CAB = ∠CBA. With CO = a sinθ ≈ aθ and AO = BO = a cosθ ≈ a, the spring angle is 2θ and the spring moment is 2Eeθ (previous page). (2) Introduces the reactions needed to keep the configuration. These are a horizontal force A at the top end (unknown), a vertical support force 2M at the base B, and a horizontal force B at the base (unknown). (3) Locates the combined centre of gravity G of the two bars. Each bar's midpoint lies at horizontal offset ½aθ from AB, so G lies on CO with OG = ½aθ, and the resultant weight 2M acts along the vertical Gg. (4) Begins the equilibrium conditions. Horizontal force balance gives A + B = C, vertical forces balance, and the internal spring forces at E and e cancel. On the next page, moments about A give 2aB + Maθ = Ca, hence A = ½C + ½Mθ and B = ½C − ½Mθ. Moment balance of bar CA about C then gives ½aC + Maθ = 2Eeθ. With C = 0, a nontrivial θ exists only when Ma = 2Ee: the critical weight of the discrete 'two-link' column.
errors: None of substance. The notation 'vi BO = 2M' uses the segment BO only to indicate the direction (vertical, upward) of the reaction, not its magnitude. This is a notational looseness, not an error.
OG = ½aθ is correct: the combined centre of mass of the two symmetric bars lies on the horizontal CO at half its length, to first order.

ideas.what: Discrete rigid-bar/rotational-spring model of a heavy column (two hinged rigid links with an elastic joint) as a surrogate for the continuous elastic column
ideas.modern_name: Rigid-link (bar–spring) buckling model; Hencky-type discrete column
ideas.usually_credited_to: Common in 20th-century stability texts (e.g. discrete models in Ziegler, Hencky chains 1920s); Euler's use here is noted in Truesdell's account of E510 / Euler's buckling papers (unsure of detail)
ideas.where_published: E510, Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778 (pub. 1780), §§7–11

ideas.what: Small-angle linearization and statics: support reactions, horizontal force balance, location of the centre of gravity
ideas.where_published: E510 and many Euler mechanics works

deep.surprise_reason: This page is routine statics setting up Euler's known discrete two-bar model of a column loaded by its own weight. The model itself is part of the published E510 and is discussed in histories of elastic stability; nothing on this page appears to be missing from the record.
